limitations: Assessment: a straightforward callback loop does not preserve the existing contract unless it reproduces per-visitor control state, handler selection, ordering, and edit short-circuiting. Executable-document validation already composes rule visitors with visitInParallel and wraps the result with visitWithTypeInfo; SDL validation already uses visitInParallel directly (src/validation/validate.ts:171-181,193-209). Combining genuinely separate full-document passes also changes their callback interleaving from pass-by-pass to node-by-node, so equivalence requires assumptions about shared state and observable ordering.

The walker performs depth-first enter/children/leave traversal using QueryDocumentKeys by default, with optional custom child keys. Arrays organize traversal but do not receive visitor callbacks. Callbacks receive node, key, parent, path, and ancestors, with this bound to the supplied visitor (src/language/visitor.ts:261-338,367-380). Preserve these arguments, child ordering, and custom-key behavior.

For an ordinary visit, undefined continues without replacement; false on enter skips descendants and that node's leave, while false on leave is not an edit. BREAK is an identity sentinel that immediately exits the entire walk. Other defined results are edits: AST-node replacements become the nodes whose children are traversed without another enter dispatch at that position; null and other non-node replacements bypass descendants and leave. Arrays are copied and null entries spliced out; object edits copy the object and assign the replacement, including null (src/language/visitor.ts:100-101,284-360,367-387). BREAK does not unwind pending ancestor leave callbacks, so preservation of pending edits must not be assumed.

visitInParallel caches each visitor's handlers by node kind and invokes active visitors in input order on both enter and leave; leave order is not reversed. Handler calls retain each original visitor as this. Enter false records the current node as that visitor's skip boundary; descendants and its boundary leave are suppressed, and it resumes when leave receives the identical boundary node. BREAK disables only that visitor permanently. These signals are consumed so other visitors continue; leave false is ignored (src/language/visitor.ts:423-475). Real rules depend on independent skipping, including NoUnusedFragmentsRule and NoFragmentCyclesRule (src/validation/rules/NoUnusedFragmentsRule.ts:54-81; src/validation/rules/NoFragmentCyclesRule.ts:61-66).

Edits are order-sensitive: the first defined result other than the locally consumed control signals returns immediately from the merged callback, preventing later visitors from receiving that enter or leave event (src/language/visitor.ts:445-470). A later visitor does not receive a replacement's enter at the same position, but can receive its descendants and eventual leave because the walker traverses the replacement (src/language/visitor.ts:349-359,370-378). Calling every visitor after an edit, feeding replacements through remaining callbacks, or isolating edits per pass would change existing behavior.

There is an additional edit/skip compatibility hazard inferred from the implementation: skip boundaries use object identity, while child edits can cause the walker to copy a skipped ancestor before its leave callback. The copied node cannot match the recorded boundary, leaving that visitor skipped beyond the intended subtree. Replacing or deleting the boundary itself can likewise prevent reset, and an earlier leave edit can prevent later reset checks from running (src/language/visitor.ts:292-313,451-456,461-473). Independent skipping is therefore not an unconditional guarantee when passes edit nodes; regression checks must expose this interaction before deciding whether to preserve or intentionally change it.

Handler selection gives a kind-specific object complete precedence over generic handlers. A kind-specific function supplies enter only; otherwise generic enter and leave are used. A missing phase in a kind-specific handler does not fall back to the generic phase. Both visit and visitInParallel select handlers before traversal, so dynamic handler mutation must not silently gain different behavior in a refactor (src/language/visitor.ts:266-269,429-438,499-517).

The type-aware wrapper enters TypeInfo before invoking enter handlers and invokes leave handlers before removing their type state. Any defined enter result first removes the original node's state and enters the replacement state only if the result is an AST node (src/utilities/TypeInfo.ts:936-966). Preserve the existing wrapper outside visitInParallel: per-rule false and BREAK are consumed internally, allowing TypeInfo to continue tracking the shared traversal. Moving the wrapper or sharing its mutable state across independently wrapped visitors requires specific checks of field, parent, argument, input, and fragment type state.

Executable validation must retain its tracing entry point, invalid-schema assertion, rule construction order, context options, and description-excluding child-key map (src/validation/validate.ts:48-53,129-173). Errors are delivered through context.reportError to the configured callback, rather than collected from visitor return values (src/validation/ValidationContext.ts:77-79; src/validation/validate.ts:158-168). The default maxErrors is 100; the next reporting attempt after the limit throws a shared sentinel, which is appended to the returned errors. The fragment-work abort sentinel is also appended, while unrelated exceptions propagate. Rule construction occurs outside the traversal try/catch (src/validation/validate.ts:149-189). Preserve error order and truncation: specifiedRules is deliberately ordered for error presentation (src/validation/specifiedRules.ts:92-131).

SDL validation uses SDLValidationContext, the optional schema being extended, specifiedSDLRules, and the default traversal keys. It has no TypeInfo wrapper, executable description filter, maxErrors option, or traversal exception catch (src/validation/validate.ts:193-209). Preserve the schema-building integration: assertion wrappers call validateSDL, and buildASTSchema and extendSchema invoke those wrappers unless assumeValid or assumeValidSDL bypasses validation (src/validation/validate.ts:218-238; src/utilities/buildASTSchema.ts:63-79; src/utilities/extendSchema.ts:150-165). Those convenience wrappers are intentionally excluded from claims.

Editing validation visitors is not a complete transformation pipeline: validateImpl and validateSDL discard visit's returned AST, while their contexts retain the original document and cache fragment or variable information (src/validation/validate.ts:177-189,207-209; src/validation/ValidationContext.ts:65-98,408-445). The high-level GraphQL pipeline validates through the harness and executes the original document when validation succeeds (src/harness.ts:50-55; src/graphql.ts:261-295). Mutating or replacing nodes during validation can therefore disagree with context lookups and subsequent execution. Also, one shared outer walk does not eliminate all internal scans: getVariableUsages performs a separately typed visit and fragment helpers perform additional graph work (src/validation/ValidationContext.ts:101-165,408-445,492-510).

Necessary regression checks include callback traces for generic and kind-specific handlers, visitor this and traversal arguments, same-order enter/leave dispatch, independent nested and root skips, sibling resumption, per-visitor BREAK on both phases, and ignored leave false. Cover enter and leave replacement, kind changes, deletion, edits suppressing later callbacks, replacement descendants, immutable result construction, edit-plus-skip identity interactions, and edits before global BREAK (src/language/visitor.ts:284-387,423-517). Validation checks should cover TypeInfo state across edits and skips, exact error ordering and maxErrors boundaries, fragment-work aborts and unrelated exceptions, description exclusion, custom and empty rule lists, SDL extension context and validation bypasses, tracing, and preservation of the document passed to execution (src/utilities/TypeInfo.ts:936-966; src/validation/validate.ts:48-53,129-209; src/graphql.ts:261-295).

This was a static investigation. Declaration locations, including both visit overload signatures, were verified with the TypeScript compiler parser; behavioral conclusions were established from source bodies. No DeepThought declaration-graph tool or resource was available. No repository modules, builds, or tests were executed, no files were modified, and no network research was used.
